column1: Facts that describe family caregivers in four ways: where they live (geographic), what they do (behavioral), who they are (demographic), and their money situation (socioeconomic). One fact per row. Most facts are national survey numbers for all US family caregivers; they are not split into Audience 1 (adult child) and Audience 2 (spouse or partner).

column2: Fact
40% of caregivers live with the person; 35% live within 20 minutes; more than 10% live an hour or more away
Urban 35%, suburban 44%, rural 20%
Forum threads that say where they live: 22 apart, 20 together
44% are in high-intensity care; average 27 hours a week; 24% give 40 or more
70% monitor the person's health; only 58% find coordinating with providers easy
55% do medical or nursing tasks; 22% were trained
34% have no other help
Remote monitoring is used by 25%, up from 13% in 2020
Of 117 caregiving forum threads: family helps in 13, doesn't help in 14, and there's conflict in 10. Most don't say.
63 million US adults, about 24%, are caregivers
Average age 50.6; 61% women, 38% men
61% non-Hispanic white, 16% Latino or Hispanic, 13% Black, 6% Asian American, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander
Care for a parent 40%, parent-in-law 7%, spouse or partner 15%
29% have children or grandchildren under 18 at home
70% of caregivers aged 18 to 64 are employed
47% had at least one negative financial impact; about 1 in 5 report high financial strain
A little over a third stopped saving; 20% left bills unpaid or paid late; 14% could not afford basics like food
Household income: 30% under $50,000; 41% $100,000 or more; median $68,770
Willingness to pay: about 20% would pay nothing and willing payers cap near $70 a month, for monitoring
Willingness to pay: 12% would pay out of pocket
